title: Decide: should the BOLT11 decoder reject non-canonical encodings (non-zero padding bits, leading zeros in x/c/9 or the hrp amount) that cyberkrill accepts?
description:
## Outcome
A recorded owner decision on whether the BOLT11 decoder rejects non-canonical encodings that cyberkrill accepts, and which. Until this bead is closed, Phase 5 (1 of 3) accepts all of them, as cyberkrill does.

## Why this exists
The signing hash is over the string as written (owner decision, 2026-10-21; Phase 5 (1 of 3), Scope). cyberkrill's lightning-invoice 0.34.0 accepts three non-canonical classes and hashes their re-encoding instead, so on those invoices the port and cyberkrill already disagree (plan §3). Rejecting a class is a stricter-than-cyberkrill delta, so under the common follow-ups rule it is the owner's call, like the L214 wrong-length bead.

What BOLT #11 @ `1914628` says, per class:
- leading zero symbols in `x`, `c` or `9`: writers MUST be minimal (L183, L187, L203-205), and a reader SHOULD treat the invoice as invalid (L239-241);
- padding in a byte-valued field that is not canonical, either non-zero padding bits or a whole extra padding symbol in a variable-length field such as `d` (lightning-invoice's `fes_to_bytes` drops any trailing bits, `de.rs:45-50`): writers MUST pad with 0s (L208); the reader section (L212-241) says nothing;
- an hrp amount with leading zeros: writers MUST NOT (L69); a reader fails on a non-digit, a bad multiplier or a pico amount that is not a whole msat (L80-87), never on leading zeros.

No reader requirement is a MUST-reject. Other readers, from source reading on 2026-10-21 (nothing was run):
- Core Lightning `common/bolt11.c` @ `2220786`: rejects non-zero trailing bits (L55) and non-minimal `x`/`c` ("not a minimal value", L80, used at L274 and L303); rejects a `9` only when its first packed byte is zero, so some leading zero symbols pass; accepts a leading-zero amount.
- LND `zpay32` (v0.21.3 and `bfe5039`): rejects non-zero padding bits (`bech32.ConvertBits(…, false)`, `decode.go:455` and its other byte fields; a whole extra zero symbol was not checked); accepts leading zeros in `x`/`c`/`9` and in the amount. It hashes as written.
- Eclair `Bolt11Invoice.scala` (master `01384e93`, one reading only): accepts non-zero padding in `p`/`s`/`h`, rejects it in `d`/`m`/`f`; accepts the other two classes.
- lightning-invoice 0.34.0 (cyberkrill, LDK): accepts all three and hashes a re-encoding.

## Options
- **Accept all three (default).** Parity with cyberkrill on acceptance. The hash is over the bytes as written, so the signature still covers exactly what was read.
- **Reject non-canonical padding and non-minimal `x`/`c`/`9`, accept a leading-zero amount.** Follows the writer MUSTs and the L239-241 SHOULD. Core Lightning does nearly this (its `9` check is on packed bytes); LND rejects only non-zero padding bits. The two hash readings would then differ only on a leading-zero hrp amount.
- **Reject all three.**
- A strict mode as a library option, with the CLI keeping cyberkrill's acceptance.

## Scope
The decision and its close reason. If any class is rejected: Phase 5 (1 of 3)'s affected positive vectors become negative vectors with their own error class, Phase 5 (3 of 3)'s round-trip hypotheses follow the decoder, and Phase 7b's goldens for them become error-exit differences listed in README.

## Dependencies / ordering
Deferred, so no Run picks it up. It blocks nothing: Phase 5 (1 of 3) runs with the default. Deciding before Phase 5 (1 of 3) starts avoids reworking its vectors.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Closed with the owner's choice in the close reason.
- If any class is rejected, the Phase 5 (1 of 3), Phase 5 (3 of 3) and Phase 7b beads are updated to match, and plan §3's BOLT11 entry says which classes the port rejects.

## Spec refs
BOLT #11 @ `1914628` L69, L80-87, L183, L187, L203-205, L208, L212-241. lightning-invoice 0.34.0 `de.rs`, `ser.rs`. Core Lightning `common/bolt11.c` @ `2220786`. LND `zpay32/decode.go` @ `bfe5039`.

title: Decide: hash the BOLT11 data part as written (BOLT #11 L117-119) or as lightning-invoice 0.34.0 re-encodes it
description:
## Outcome
A recorded owner decision between two readings of the BOLT11 signing hash: (a) lightning-invoice 0.34.0's, for parity with cyberkrill, or (b) BOLT #11's, as written. It also settles what plan §2's `lightning` obligation "signing hash equals its spec definition" means. Phase 5 (1 of 3) cannot start until this bead is closed with the choice in its close reason, so no Run builds either reading before the owner decides.

## Why this exists
BOLT #11 @ `1914628` L117-119 defines the signing hash as SHA-256 over the human-readable part and the data part as written, with 0 bits appended to a byte boundary.

cyberkrill decodes with lightning-invoice 0.34.0 (`decoder.rs:429-432`), which hashes something else:
- `SignedRawBolt11Invoice::from_str` sets the hash to `raw_invoice.signable_hash()` (`de.rs:395`);
- that is `hash_from_parts` over the hrp printed back from its parsed parts and the data part re-encoded from the parsed timestamp and fields (`lib.rs:1084-1120`, `ser.rs:176-190`, `ser.rs:243-248`).

The two agree on every canonical invoice and on the 17 spec examples that decode: the 16 valid ones and L814. L814 is not canonical (its 52-symbol `n` is a length BOLT #11 L214 says a reader MUST fail, and the spec lists it among the invalid examples), but the crate keeps that field raw (`de.rs:517-523`) and writes it back verbatim (`ser.rs:265`). They differ on non-canonical encodings the crate accepts:
- non-zero padding bits in a byte-valued field;
- leading zero symbols in `x`, `c` or `9`;
- an hrp amount with leading zeros (`lnbc02500u` hashes as `lnbc2500u`).

With no `n` field the payee key is recovered from that hash, so on such an invoice the two readings give different payee keys. Observed through lightning-invoice 0.34.0, with a throwaway Rust harness over cyberkrill's locked crate versions run offline (cyberkrill itself was not built or run): L383 with its `p` padding bits set and its own signature decodes with hash `6daf4d48…` (L383's own) and payee `03e7156…`, the published key; re-signed over its as-written hash `142eb817…` with the spec's example key, the same invoice decodes with payee `03a0ddf5…`.

AGENTS.md "Proof hygiene" says never to weaken a theorem the plan states. Whether a theorem over the re-encoding meets plan §2's "signing hash equals its spec definition" is the owner's call, not a Run's.

## Options
**(a) Parity: hash the re-encoding, as lightning-invoice 0.34.0 does.** This is what the beads say today, and their text is the (a) text.
- Phase 5 (1 of 3): unchanged. The signing hash is computed over the encoder's output for the decoded hrp and fields. The padding vector keeps L383's signature and decodes with the published payee key. README "Deltas not taken" cites L117-119 and the padding vector.
- Phase 5 (3 of 3): unchanged. The theorem is stated over the invoice's own encoding, and equals BOLT #11's hash over the string for every string the encoder writes.
- Phase 7b: unchanged. The padding vector's golden matches cyberkrill (`destination` is the published payee key).
- plan §2: the `lightning` row's "signing hash equals its spec definition" is recorded as "over the invoice's re-encoding (lightning-invoice 0.34.0's reading), which equals BOLT #11's hash over the string on canonical strings".

**(b) Spec: hash the data part as written, per BOLT #11 L117-119.** This is a documented exception to golden parity on non-canonical invoices, like plan §3's BIP370 v2 one.
- Phase 5 (1 of 3): the decoder hashes the string's own lower-cased hrp bytes and its data symbols as written (signature excluded), with 0 bits appended to a byte boundary. The encoder hashes its own output, so the two agree on the 17 spec examples that decode. The padding vector is re-signed over its as-written hash by the vector script (so 3 re-signed positive vectors, each in the test table), and decodes with the published payee key. README "Deltas taken" replaces the "Deltas not taken" entry, citing L117-119 and the padding vector.
- Phase 5 (3 of 3): the signing-hash criterion becomes "for every string `s` with `decode cap s = .ok inv`, the hash the decoder checks equals BOLT #11's hash over `s`'s own hrp and data part", plus the encoder's hash over `encode inv`. The re-encoding clause and its "not a weakening" note go.
- Phase 7b: the padding vector is re-signed over the as-written digest, and its golden is whatever cyberkrill prints or its exit code (through the crate, it recovers `03a0ddf5…`); the port prints the published key. That golden becomes a documented, tested exception, and README lists it.
- plan §2: the obligation stands as written. Plan §3 lists the non-canonical signing hash among the documented exceptions to golden parity.

## Scope
Settling the decision, recording it in the close reason, and editing plan.md §2 (and, for (b), §3) to record it. This is not implementation.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Phase 5 (1 of 3) waits for this bead, and through it Phase 5 (3 of 3), Phase 7a, Phase 7b and everything after. Phase 5 (2 of 3) (LNURL) has no signing hash and does not wait.
- Deferred so that no Run picks it up: it is the owner's call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Closed with the owner's choice, (a) or (b), in the close reason.
- plan.md §2's `lightning` row records the chosen reading, and the beads follow it: Phase 5 (1 of 3), Phase 5 (3 of 3) and Phase 7b as written under (a), or as the (b) list above says.

## Spec refs
BOLT #11 @ `1914628` L117-119. lightning-invoice 0.34.0 `de.rs:395`, `lib.rs:1084-1120`, `ser.rs:176-190`, `ser.rs:243-248`, `ser.rs:265`. cyberkrill `cyberkrill-core/src/decoder.rs:361-368`, `:429-432` @ `27cad1f`. Phase 5 (1 of 3), Scope ("Signing hash, as lightning-invoice computes it").

## Decision
Owner, 2026-10-21: **(b)**. Phase 5 (1 of 3), Phase 5 (3 of 3) and Phase 7b now carry the (b) text. Phase 5 (1 of 3) also tests every non-canonical class: six non-canonical positive vectors (padding bits in `p`, an extra padding symbol in `d`, a leading zero in `x`, a leading zero in `9`, a leading-zero hrp amount, and the `n`-field vector with padding bits), so eight re-signed positive vectors in all. The crate also accepts a whole extra padding symbol in a variable-length byte field (`fes_to_bytes` drops trailing bits) and re-encodes it shorter, so that is non-canonical padding too. Plan §3 lists the exception; plan §2's obligation is unchanged. Rejecting non-canonical encodings is a separate deferred `owner-decision` bead.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-21: (b), the spec's rule. The signing hash is SHA-256 over the invoice's own lower-cased hrp and its data part as written (BOLT #11 L117-119), as LND and Core Lightning compute it. Where this differs from cyberkrill's lightning-invoice 0.34.0, which hashes a re-encoding, it is a documented, tested exception to golden parity, like BIP370 v2 PSBTs: plan.md section 3 lists it and README lists it when Phase 5 lands. Plan section 2's obligation 'signing hash equals its spec definition' stands as written. Phase 5 (1 of 3) lck-phase-5-lightning-50n, Phase 5 (3 of 3) lck-phase-5c-bolt11-proofs-vs2 and Phase 7b lck-phase-7b-ln-offline-commands-rp1 carry the (b) text. Rejecting non-canonical encodings is the deferred owner-decision bead 'Decide: should the BOLT11 decoder reject non-canonical encodings'.

title: Decide: does onchain-move-utxos keep cyberkrill's --max-amount overpay (excess goes to the miner)?
description:
## Outcome
**Decided (owner, 2026-10-19); see the close reason. plan.md §3 records it, and Phase 8c (2 of 2) implements it.** The rest of this bead is the question as it stood before the decision.

A recorded owner decision on whether the port reproduces a cyberkrill behaviour that pays any selected amount above `--max-amount` to the miner as extra fee. Phase 8c cannot start until this bead is closed with the decision in its close reason. The decision must also go into plan.md §3.

## Why this exists
Plan §3 says to port the local fee and selection exactly. In cyberkrill @ `27cad1f`, on the RPC path of `move_utxos` (`cyberkrill-core/src/bitcoin_rpc.rs`):
1. inputs are selected largest first while `--max-amount` is set (`:1329-1345`);
2. then `total = selected.min(max)` (`:1354`);
3. and the single output is `total - fee` (`:1390`, `:1401`).

There is no change output. Every selected input is still spent, so whatever was selected above `max` becomes fee. For example, UTXOs of 0.6 and 0.5 BTC with max 1.0 overpay the miner by 0.1 BTC. cyberkrill's BDK path (`bdk_wallet.rs:854-900`) spends the whole selection instead, so there `max` is only a soft limit.

v1 never signs or broadcasts, but a user who signs the resulting PSBT loses the excess.

## Options
1. Port exactly: bug-compatible, documented in README.
2. Fix it in the port:
   - add a change output back to the source, or
   - select only up to `max` and spend the selection in full (the BDK path's behaviour);
   - and document the difference from cyberkrill.
3. Refuse when the selection exceeds `max` by more than the fee.

## Scope
Settling the decision, and editing plan.md §3 to record it. This is not implementation.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Blocked Phase 8c (2 of 2) until closed.
- It was deferred so that no Run picked it up, as the owner's call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Closed with the owner's choice in the close reason.
- plan.md §3 updated.

## Spec refs
plan.md §3 (Local weight and fee estimation). cyberkrill `cyberkrill-core/src/bitcoin_rpc.rs:1329-1401` and `cyberkrill-core/src/bdk_wallet.rs:854-900` @ `27cad1f`.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-19: keep cyberkrill's largest-first selection, but the onchain-move-utxos output is the full selected total minus the fee, with no clamp to --max-amount, so the excess is never silently given to the miner. This matches cyberkrill's BDK path and is a documented, tested difference from its Core path (bitcoin_rpc.rs:1354, 1390, 1401), reported upstream as douglaz/cyberkrill#152. Implemented by Phase 8c (2 of 2), lck-phase-8c-move-utxos-xxl; recorded in plan.md sections 3 and 4.

title: Decide: how PSBT RIPEMD-160 and HASH160 preimage checks are hashed (plan gap found during bead transfer)
description:
## Outcome
**Decided (owner, 2026-10-19); see the close reason. plan.md §1 records it, and Phase 4a (2 of 3) implements it.** The rest of this bead is the question as it stood before the decision.

A recorded owner decision on one point plan.md leaves open: how the copied PSBT field parser checks `PSBT_IN_RIPEMD160` and `PSBT_IN_HASH160` preimages, once the `LeanHash160` import is cut. Phase 4a cannot start until this bead is closed with the decision in its close reason. The decision must also go into plan.md §1.

## Why this exists
The plan (§1, lean-miniscript row) says: copy `Psbt/Codec.lean` and `Psbt/Fields.lean`, "drop its `Secp256k1`/`LeanHash160` imports; hash through `sha256`".

But `LeanMiniscript/Psbt/Fields.lean` @ `cb9bc5f` lines 272-276 (`preimageHash`) also hashes preimages with:
- `LeanHash160.RIPEMD160.hash` for key type `inRipemd160`;
- `LeanHash160.hash160` for key type `inHash160` (`Fields.lean:49`).

The decoder validates the 20-byte preimage fields at `Fields.lean:401-411`.

RIPEMD-160 is in no package the plan lists. lean4-hash @ `ab7eda4` carries only SHA-256 and SHA-3. So "hash through sha256" cannot cover these two key types.

## Options considered
1. **Copy RIPEMD-160** from `febyeji/lean-hash160` @ `d55f386`:
   - Apache-2.0, adapted from powdr-labs/evm-semantics; about 350 lines including its SHA-256; no Mathlib.
   - It would go into `sha256` or `bitcoin` with its NOTICE beside it, tested against the published RIPEMD-160 vectors, with no proof obligation at level M.
2. **Write our own RIPEMD-160**, tested against the published vectors.
3. **Do not verify** RIPEMD-160 and HASH160 preimages. Accept the fields as upstream framing allows, keep the SHA-256 and HASH256 checks, and document the difference.
4. **Supply them as a capability** next to the pubkey check (FFI-backed).

## Scope
Settling the decision, and editing plan.md §1 to record it. This is not implementation.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Blocked Phase 4a (2 of 3) until closed.
- It was deferred so that no Run picked it up, as the owner's call.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Closed with the owner's choice in the close reason.
- plan.md §1 updated in the same branch as the next plan edit.

## Spec refs
plan.md §1 (lean-miniscript decision), §2 (`bitcoin` row, PSBT). Upstream: `LeanMiniscript/Psbt/Fields.lean` @ `cb9bc5f` L49, L207, L272-276, L401-411.
close_reason: Owner decision 2026-10-19: write our own RIPEMD-160, and HASH160 = RIPEMD-160(SHA-256), in the bitcoin package: about 130 lines under the repo's MIT OR Apache-2.0 header, tested against the published RIPEMD-160 test vectors. lean-hash160 is not copied (it is Apache-2.0 only). The PSBT RIPEMD160/HASH160 preimage checks go through it, matching rust-bitcoin 0.32.8, which rejects bad preimages. Implemented by Phase 4a (2 of 3), lck-phase-4a-ripemd160-hash160-bq5; recorded in plan.md sections 1, 2 and 4.

title: Phase 0: CI green on a pull request
description:
## Outcome
The `CI` workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `check`) passes on a pull request into `master`. That closes the last open item of Phase 0's definition of done.

## Why this exists
Plan §4, Phase 0 DoD: "CI green on a PR". The bootstrap commit `d010262` went straight to `master` with owner approval. Its CI run (`39315028103`, success) was a push run, not a PR run. The pull request that adds this bead graph (`chore/beads`) is the first PR, so it doubles as this check.

## Scope
- Open the bead-graph PR and watch its CI run.
- If CI fails for a workflow or environment reason, fix that on the PR branch. Check runner disk space first: the toolchain is about 3 GB unpacked and the derivation copies it.

## Non-goals
- No package, flake or plan changes beyond what a CI failure forces.
- Not rloop work. rloop never pushes or opens PRs, so whoever opens the bead-graph PR closes this bead.

## Dependencies / ordering
None. Nothing depends on this bead. Close it as soon as the PR's CI run is green, before any Run branch is cut from the bead branch.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `gh pr checks <pr>` shows `check` passing, and `gh run view <run-id> --json conclusion` prints `success`.
- Close with a reason that names the PR number, the run id and the commit it tested.

## Spec refs
plan.md §4 (Phase 0 row); `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.
close_reason: CI green on PR #1: GitHub Actions run 39501429993 (pull_request, check job) succeeded on 3350427.

title: Phase 10a (3 of 3): licence and Reservoir re-check, package split table, and upstream patches
description:
## Outcome
The evidence that Phase 10b's owner decisions need, gathered without any outward-facing action:
- the licence and Reservoir metadata, re-checked for v1;
- a split recommendation for each package;
- the fixes in `docs/upstream-fixes.md`, turned into ready local patches.

## Why this exists
The owner decides going public, package splits, Reservoir publication and upstream submissions (Phase 10b). This bead prepares the evidence for those decisions.

## Scope
- **Licence and Reservoir checks** (plan §5), all read-only:
  - GitHub's detected licence for the repo;
  - `lake reservoir-config` for each package (`license`, `licenseFiles`);
  - Lake's single-identifier SPDX docstring trade-off, re-checked against the then-current Lake and Reservoir;
  - the third-party notices the **static release binary** needs, derived from Phase 10a (2 of 3)'s link evidence (the archives on its link line), each library with its licence in README. Expect at least: the Lean 4 runtime and core libraries (`libleanrt`, `Init`, `Std`, `Lean`; Apache-2.0), musl libc (MIT), mimalloc (MIT) if linked, `libgmp.a` (LGPL-3.0-or-later or GPL-2.0-or-later), OpenSSL's `libssl.a`/`libcrypto.a`, `libuv.a`, the C++ runtime it links, libsecp256k1, libcurl and every static dependency of libcurl, and the MIT notices of the copied lean4-hash and lean-miniscript code, the BIP39 English wordlist that `generate-mnemonic` embeds (bitcoin/bips @ `130b8e0` `bip-0039/english.txt`, MIT per BIP39's header), and lean4-cli whenever the app uses it (vendored or through a flake input: either way it is compiled into the binary).
  - README lists, for Phase 10b, the obligation each one carries, in particular LGPL-3.0's relinking requirement for the statically linked `libgmp.a` (relinkable objects or another route). Phase 10b's owner decides it.
- **Split recommendation.** For each package: dependencies, size, and the cost of splitting it out of the monorepo. One table.
- **Upstream patches.** Turn each entry in `docs/upstream-fixes.md` into a local patch file or branch against lean-miniscript @ `cb9bc5f`, lean4-hash @ `ab7eda4`, or lean4-cli at the tag Phase 7a pinned (only if Phase 7a vendored it and logged fixes), each with a one-line rationale. **Do not open upstream PRs.**

## Non-goals
- Changing repo visibility, publishing to Reservoir, pushing to other repositories or opening upstream PRs. All of these are outward-facing and the owner's (Phase 10b).
- The static build (Phase 10a, 1 and 2 of 3).

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- `gh` and `lake` calls are read-only.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on every other v1 bead: both Phase 3b beads, and the last bead of each chain (Phases 8b, both 8c beads, 9a (2 of 2), 9b, 9c, 9d, and through them the rest).
- Also depends on Phase 10a (2 of 3): the notices come from the static binary's link evidence.
- Phase 10b waits for this bead.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The licence check outputs are recorded.
- The split table is in the repo.
- Each `docs/upstream-fixes.md` entry has a patch, and the patch list is in the repo or the Run report.
### Common definition of done (plan §4, every Run)
- `nix build` and `nix flake check` exit 0. The flake check runs `lake build && lake test` for every package listed in `lakePackages` in `flake.nix`, inside the nix sandbox, then runs the app. Stage new files (`git add`) before running `nix flake check`: a flake sees only tracked files.
- In each touched package, `nix develop -c lake build` and `nix develop -c lake test` exit 0.
- No `sorry`: `grep -rnw sorry --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake packages` prints nothing (CI runs the same check from Phase 2 on).
- `#print axioms` on every theorem this bead lists shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Each listed theorem is added to the package's committed axiom-gate test (Phase 2's pattern); `lake test` fails on any axiom outside the three. The gate is an allowlist of those three and contains no "sorry" substring. No `native_decide` in library or proof modules; test files may use it.
- The vector counts this bead states pass. Each test asserts that the number of vectors it loaded equals a pinned constant, so a dropped vector fails, and the test output prints each count (for example `<set> valid: N/N`).
- `README.md` is updated: what the package now provides, vector sources and counts, and anything this bead says to document.
- `AGENTS.md` rules hold, including "Reference only" for any value taken from cyberkrill. New Lean, C and script files we write carry the dual-licence header; third-party and copied files follow the rule below, and JSON and other formats without comments need none.
- **Safety.** Tests use only published vectors, published test mnemonics, the BOLT #11 specification's published example private key (tests only), recordings from a throwaway regtest node, and synthetic or script-generated fixtures under the third-party rule (for example cyberkrill's captured outputs on those inputs, synthetic provider responses, our own LNURL and LUD JSON, values a committed script derives from published inputs). Never anything from the owner's node, wallets or devices. Tests never reach the internet, port 8332 or `~/.bitcoin`. Nothing committed contains private keys, seeds, xprvs, tprvs or WIF keys, or real addresses, xpubs or device dumps, apart from that BOLT #11 example key. No hardware wallets, no signing outside test vectors, no broadcast, no mainnet funds.
- **Third-party material** (`AGENTS.md` "Licence", plan §5):
  - Admitted in the tree, each with a provenance sidecar or header line (source URL, commit, path, licence), never the dual-licence header: MIT, BSD, ISC, CC0 or public domain, and CC-BY-4.0 (attribution and a note of any changes, for example "extracted and reformatted", kept in the sidecar). Material offered under a choice that includes MIT (such as fedimint-lite's `MIT OR Apache-2.0`) is taken under MIT.
  - Kept out of the tree: Apache-2.0-only, share-alike (CC-BY-SA) and unlicensed material. Use a pinned non-flake input read at test time, or replace it with vectors we generate ourselves.
  - Copied code whose upstream file has no header gets a provenance comment (upstream repo, commit, path, "MIT") with the upstream MIT notice in a file beside it, never the dual-licence header.
  - In a Lean file the provenance line is the first line and a `--` line comment (or `/- … -/`), never a `/-! … -/` doc comment, for example `-- Copied from <repo> @ <commit>, <path>; MIT, see <notice file>`. JSON and other formats without comments get the sidecar.
- **Stop mechanics.** If this bead says stop and report: commit no weakened statement, `br defer` the bead, add label `owner-decision`, comment what was tried (`br comments add`), and end the Run blocked.
- **Follow-ups.** A delta or stricter check you think v1 needs goes in a new bead created deferred with label `owner-decision`, and in README "Deltas not taken". Never implement it unranked.
- **Upstream fixes.** A fix that would also help upstream (lean4-hash, lean-miniscript) goes in the committed `docs/upstream-fixes.md` (file, problem, fix), not in a br comment. Phase 10a (3 of 3) turns that file into patches.

## Spec refs
plan.md §1 (Layout; Visibility; lean-miniscript), §4 (Phase 10 row), §5 (re-check at v1).

title: Phase 10a (2 of 3): static cyberkrill binary, one-OpenSSL symbol check, and a run in an empty root without nix
description:
## Outcome
A reproducible **static** musl build of the `cyberkrill` binary, as a separate flake output, shown to contain exactly one OpenSSL and to run in an empty root directory with no `/nix`, `/lib` or `/usr`.

## Why this exists
The public v1 should match cyberkrill's static release binaries (plan §1 Toolchain, §3).

## Scope
- **Static binary.** Build it with Phase 10a (1 of 3)'s toolchain. Link static libsecp256k1 and libcurl, with **exactly one** static OpenSSL (plan §3).
- **Symbol check.** `ldd` says "not a dynamic executable", so show the single OpenSSL from the binary's symbols and the archives it links. Extend `scripts/check-one-openssl.sh` with a static mode if that fits.
- **No-nix check.** This host has no container runtime (`command -v docker podman` prints nothing) and no `bwrap`. Run the static binary in an empty root that holds only the binary, a test CA and the stub's files: no `/nix`, `/lib` or `/usr`.

title: Phase 1a (2 of 2): secp256k1 C adapter and Lean bindings (parse, verify, recover, sign) with vectors
description:
## Outcome
`packages/secp256k1` is a working Lake package. A small C adapter over nix's libsecp256k1 (0.8.0 at the pinned nixpkgs, recovery module on), linked through Phase 1a (1 of 2)'s target, exposes four operations to Lean:
1. Parse a public key (33-byte compressed or 65-byte uncompressed) and report whether it is valid.
2. ECDSA verify of a 64-byte compact (r‖s) signature, the form Phase 5's capability passes; the matching Wycheproof set is the P1363 file.
3. Recover a public key from a 64-byte compact signature plus a recovery id (0-3) and a 32-byte message hash.
4. Recoverable, deterministic (RFC 6979) signing of a 32-byte hash, returning the 64-byte compact signature and the recovery id.

## Why this exists
- The plan chose crypto path A (owner decision, 2026-10-19). libsecp256k1 does every curve operation behind one small Lean interface, so a verified implementation can replace it after v1.
- Pure packages need these operations as supplied capabilities: the PSBT pubkey check (Phase 4a), and BOLT11 recovery, verification and signing (Phase 5). The app wires them in Phase 7a.

## Scope
- C adapter and Lean `@[extern]` bindings in `packages/secp256k1` only. C lives only in `secp256k1` and `http-curl` (plan §1).
- Switch the `Secp256k1Tests` test driver from a built-only `lean_lib` to a `lean_exe`, so `lake test` actually runs the vectors.
- Document the Lean interface in the package (doc comments plus a README section): signatures, byte layouts, error cases. A replacement implementation must be able to satisfy it.
- Tests decode hex vectors with a small **test-only** hex helper. The library hex codec belongs to Phase 3a (1 of 4); do not add one to `secp256k1`.

## Non-goals
- The link targets and the OpenSSL resolution (Phase 1a, 1 of 2).
- The curl wrapper (Phase 1b). SHA-256 (Phase 2): tests use precomputed 32-byte message hashes, and the Wycheproof digests come from the nix build step below. `secp256k1` gains no Lean dependency (plan §2), and its tests link no OpenSSL for hashing.
- The capability structures that pure packages consume. `bitcoin` and `lightning` define those (Phases 4a and 5); the app fills them (Phase 7a).
- Schnorr/BIP340, key generation, and anything not listed above.
- Entropy for `generate-mnemonic`. Phase 7a decides whether a `getrandom` C call must be added here.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Every FFI call returns a Lean-side error value for bad input (wrong length, invalid key, recid out of range, unparsable signature). None may crash the process.

- Signing exists only for test vectors in v1. The only private key the tests may use is the BOLT #11 specification's published example key. No other key material is committed.
- **RFC 6979 check first.** Before writing the signing vectors, sign one low-S BOLT #11 example's digest (not the high-S one below) and compare the result with the spec's signature.
- **High-S example, confirmed through the binding first.** The valid example under "Public-key recovery with high-S signature" (`11-payment-encoding.md` L762) is the only one of the 16 valid examples with s > n/2. Before writing the recovery vectors, recover it through this binding (libsecp256k1 does not normalise s) and pin the key it returns. Off-line, with nix libsecp256k1 0.8.0 through a Python binding, it gave `02d0139ce7427d6dfffd26a326c18be754ef1e64672b42694ba5b23ef6e6e7803d`, not the payee key. If the binding returns another key, pin what libsecp256k1 says, use it in this bead's ACs, and note it in README for Phase 5 (1 of 3)'s lookup table. If it differs, the signing acceptance becomes sign → recover → verify for every example instead of byte equality, and README says why.
- **Wycheproof is Apache-2.0 only** (GitHub's licence for C2SP/wycheproof). Committing its JSON would make `secp256k1` "(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Apache-2.0", the problem Phase 4a (2 of 3) avoids for RIPEMD-160.
  - Take the file through a pinned non-flake input, `inputs.wycheproof = { url = "github:C2SP/wycheproof/7a325932231bd7a724c791c8b0d65ea4d6d2f435"; flake = false; }`, passed to the check derivation and the dev shell (for example through an environment variable the tests read). Commit no Wycheproof file, and no file derived from one.
  - **Digests.** Wycheproof ECDSA entries carry `msg`, not its hash, and libsecp256k1 exports no plain SHA-256. Compute the digests in a nix build step: a `runCommand` derivation runs python3's `hashlib.sha256` over each `msg` of the pinned input's JSON and writes `tcId digest` lines. Pass its output path to the check derivation **and** the dev shell, so host-side `lake test` reads it too. Commit no derived file.
  - If that cannot work, stop and report, and raise a deferred `owner-decision` bead.

- Depends on Phase 1a (1 of 2): the link target and the OpenSSL resolution.
- Phase 1b and Phase 7a wait for both Phase 1a beads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **Recovery vectors.** For each BOLT #11 specification example (`11-payment-encoding.md` at lightning/bolts @ `191462825ae341f0a27098765c075f01ca9bc6c2`), recover the published payee key `03e7156ae33b0a208d0744199163177e909e80176e55d97a2f221ede0f934dd9ad` from its 65-byte signature, for the 15 low-S examples. Hash the signing preimage (SHA-256 over the lower-cased hrp bytes plus the data part; the all-upper-case example at L704 carries the same signature as L683's invoice) ahead of time, with a committed generator script that uses a nix-provided tool, and check in the resulting 32-byte digests.   - State the counts, including invalid cases rejected. Where the file marks a high-S signature valid, count it as an expected reject and say so in README.

title: Phase 1a (1 of 2): Lake FFI link targets for libsecp256k1 and libcurl, and the one-OpenSSL link spike
description:
## Outcome
`packages/secp256k1` and `packages/http-curl` each ship a Lake link target for their nix C library. A **link spike** proves the hard part of Phase 1b early: one executable links libsecp256k1 **and** the real nix libcurl through those targets, and contains exactly one OpenSSL. A committed `scripts/check-one-openssl.sh` checks that, and `nix flake check` runs it.

The curl wrapper is not written yet. Calling something trivial is enough, such as `curl_version()` and creating a libsecp256k1 context.

## Why this exists
- The OpenSSL duplication risk must be settled before the HTTPS work starts, and the link mechanics before any binding is written.
- Phase 1a is split in two to keep each Run small. The C adapter, Lean bindings and vectors are Phase 1a (2 of 2).

## Scope
- **Versions.** Re-read every version from `flake.lock` and the pinned nixpkgs, and record them in README. At the time of transfer:
  - nixpkgs `fe13242` has libsecp256k1 **0.8.0**, with the recovery module on;
  - nix curl 8.22.0 links OpenSSL **3.5.8**;
  - the toolchain's static OpenSSL is **3.6.0**.
  - Confirm that nixpkgs' `secp256k1` is built with the recovery module. If it is not, override it in the flake.
- **Lake build.** Lake v4.35 deprecates `extern_lib`. Use a custom target with `moreLinkObjs`/`moreLinkLibs` (Lake README @ v4.35.0).
  - An executable gets its dependencies' link objects and libraries, but only the **root** package's raw link flags: `recComputeModuleLinkInfo` (`Lake/Build/Module.lean` L1299-1337; root `linkArgs` at L1334-1336) and `Build/Executable.lean` L20-29.
  - So each FFI package ships its own link targets: the libsecp256k1 one in `packages/secp256k1`, the libcurl one in `packages/http-curl`.
- **nix.** Add libsecp256k1 and curl to the dev shell and to the sandboxed check derivation in `flake.nix`. Any new package or executable must appear in `lakePackages`, or `nix flake check` skips it.
  - The check's source is only `lean-toolchain` and `packages/` (`flake.nix:63`), so add `./scripts` to its `fileset`, or keep the script under `packages/`.
  - Its `nativeBuildInputs` is only `lean` (`flake.nix:65`), and stdenv's path has no `ldd`. Add `pkgs.glibc.bin` (for `ldd`) and `pkgs.binutils` (for `nm`, `readelf`) if they are not already on the path, or use `readelf -d` / `patchelf --print-needed`.
  - Run the script in `buildPhase`, after the package loop, on the spike executable's path and on the app binary's.
  - `lake build` builds only default targets, and `packages/cyberkrill/lakefile.lean` marks only `lean_exe cyberkrill` `@[default_target]`. Build the spike in `buildPhase` with `lake build linkspike` (or mark it `@[default_target]`) before running the script on `.lake/build/bin/linkspike`.
- **Spike location.** The spike is a `lean_exe linkspike` (root `LinkSpike`) in `packages/cyberkrill`, the only package that requires both FFI packages (`packages/cyberkrill/lakefile.lean`). An executable gets only the root package's raw link flags, so a spike there links the way the shipping binary does.
  - Each FFI package ships its own link target and a one-function C shim: `curl_version()` in `http-curl`, and context create/destroy in `secp256k1`.
  - No FFI package requires the other (plan §2: both have no Lean deps).
- **`scripts/check-one-openssl.sh`.** It takes an executable's path and exits non-zero unless exactly one OpenSSL provider remains. It fails when any of these holds:
  - (a) the dynamic closure (`ldd`, or `readelf -d` followed recursively) holds more than one libssl or more than one libcrypto;
  - (b) the executable itself defines OpenSSL symbols (`nm --defined-only`, and `nm -D --defined-only`, match `/ [TtDdRrBb] (SSL_|OPENSSL_|EVP_|CRYPTO_)/`) while its closure also holds a libssl;
  - (c) more than one distinct `OpenSSL [0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+` version string appears across the executable and its closure (scan the bytes with `grep -aoE`).
  - The flake check runs it on `packages/cyberkrill/.lake/build/bin/linkspike` **and** on the app binary `packages/cyberkrill/.lake/build/bin/cyberkrill`, from this bead on. `packages/cyberkrill/Cyberkrill.lean:10` already imports `HttpCurl` and `Main.lean:5` imports `Cyberkrill`, so once this bead attaches the libcurl link target to `http-curl`, the shipping binary's import closure reaches it. Record the app binary's `readelf -d` output in README. No later bead adds this run.
  - Why three checks: the toolchain's `lib/` ships only static `libssl.a`/`libcrypto.a` (OpenSSL 3.6.0) and `leanc --print-ldflags` puts `-lssl -lcrypto` inside an `--as-needed` group (`-Wl,--as-needed -lgmp -luv -lssl -lcrypto -lpthread -ldl -lrt -Wl,--no-as-needed …`), while nix curl NEEDs `libssl.so.3` (3.5.8). The duplicate to catch is a static 3.6.0 copy beside curl's dynamic one, and `ldd` still shows one `libssl.so.3` then.

- The C adapter, Lean bindings and vectors (Phase 1a, 2 of 2).
- The curl wrapper, HTTP API and CA handling (Phase 1b).

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- **Exactly one OpenSSL.** Lean 4.35 only puts OpenSSL on the link line: its runtime hooks are stubs, and the flags depend on Lean's build configuration (`src/CMakeLists.txt` L416-425 @ v4.35.0).
  - The spike executable must contain exactly one libssl/libcrypto. Resolve it by building curl against the toolchain's OpenSSL, or the reverse.
  - Record in README which way was chosen, and the `ldd`/`nm` evidence.
  - **If neither direction links, stop and report**, with the `ldd` output of each attempt.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on Phase 0, which is done: the bootstrap, and CI green on PR #1 (the CI-on-PR bead is closed).
- Phase 1a (2 of 2) waits for this bead. Phase 1b and Phase 7a wait for both Phase 1a beads.
- Runs first in the plan's order (0 → 1a → 1b → 2 → 3a → …).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The spike executable builds inside `nix flake check` and calls into both libraries.
- `scripts/check-one-openssl.sh` passes on it there, and on the app binary `cyberkrill`; the app binary's `readelf -d` output is in README.
- **Red fixture** (AGENTS.md: a test that never failed proves nothing). A variant of the spike whose C shim calls `OpenSSL_version(0)`, linked so that `-lssl`/`-lcrypto` resolve to the toolchain's archives (for example `libcrypto.a` under `-Wl,--whole-archive`). The script must fail it, on (b) or (c); paste that failing output into README. Its C shim lives under `packages/http-curl/test/` (or is built as a nix derivation from a file there), and the flake's red-fixture run of `scripts/check-one-openssl.sh` consumes it from there; no C file goes into `packages/cyberkrill` (plan §1: C code only in `secp256k1` and `http-curl`).
- **Link evidence.** The `ldd`, `nm` and version-string output for the spike executable, pasted into README. "No static copy pulled in" is a valid green outcome only if that `nm` and version-string evidence is there.
- README records the versions read from `flake.lock` and which OpenSSL direction was chosen.
### Common definition of done (plan §4, every Run)
- `nix build` and `nix flake check` exit 0. The flake check runs `lake build && lake test` for every package listed in `lakePackages` in `flake.nix`, inside the nix sandbox, then runs the app. Stage new files (`git add`) before running `nix flake check`: a flake sees only tracked files.
- In each touched package, `nix develop -c lake build` and `nix develop -c lake test` exit 0.
- No `sorry`: `grep -rnw sorry --include='*.lean' --exclude-dir=.lake packages` prints nothing (CI runs the same check from Phase 2 on).
- `#print axioms` on every theorem this bead lists shows only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. Each listed theorem is added to the package's committed axiom-gate test (Phase 2's pattern); `lake test` fails on any axiom outside the three. The gate is an allowlist of those three and contains no "sorry" substring. No `native_decide` in library or proof modules; test files may use it.
- The vector counts this bead states pass. Each test asserts that the number of vectors it loaded equals a pinned constant, so a dropped vector fails, and the test output prints each count (for example `<set> valid: N/N`).
- `README.md` is updated: what the package now provides, vector sources and counts, and anything this bead says to document.
- `AGENTS.md` rules hold, including "Reference only" for any value taken from cyberkrill. New Lean, C and script files we write carry the dual-licence header; third-party and copied files follow the rule below, and JSON and other formats without comments need none.
- **Safety.** Tests use only published vectors, published test mnemonics, the BOLT #11 specification's published example private key (tests only), recordings from a throwaway regtest node, and synthetic or script-generated fixtures under the third-party rule (for example cyberkrill's captured outputs on those inputs, synthetic provider responses, our own LNURL and LUD JSON, values a committed script derives from published inputs). Never anything from the owner's node, wallets or devices. Tests never reach the internet, port 8332 or `~/.bitcoin`. Nothing committed contains private keys, seeds, xprvs, tprvs or WIF keys, or real addresses, xpubs or device dumps, apart from that BOLT #11 example key. No hardware wallets, no signing outside test vectors, no broadcast, no mainnet funds.
- **Third-party material** (`AGENTS.md` "Licence", plan §5):
  - Admitted in the tree, each with a provenance sidecar or header line (source URL, commit, path, licence), never the dual-licence header: MIT, BSD, ISC, CC0 or public domain, and CC-BY-4.0 (attribution and a note of any changes, for example "extracted and reformatted", kept in the sidecar). Material offered under a choice that includes MIT (such as fedimint-lite's `MIT OR Apache-2.0`) is taken under MIT.
  - Kept out of the tree: Apache-2.0-only, share-alike (CC-BY-SA) and unlicensed material. Use a pinned non-flake input read at test time, or replace it with vectors we generate ourselves.
  - Copied code whose upstream file has no header gets a provenance comment (upstream repo, commit, path, "MIT") with the upstream MIT notice in a file beside it, never the dual-licence header.
  - In a Lean file the provenance line is the first line and a `--` line comment (or `/- … -/`), never a `/-! … -/` doc comment, for example `-- Copied from <repo> @ <commit>, <path>; MIT, see <notice file>`. JSON and other formats without comments get the sidecar.
- **Stop mechanics.** If this bead says stop and report: commit no weakened statement, `br defer` the bead, add label `owner-decision`, comment what was tried (`br comments add`), and end the Run blocked.
- **Follow-ups.** A delta or stricter check you think v1 needs goes in a new bead created deferred with label `owner-decision`, and in README "Deltas not taken". Never implement it unranked.
- **Upstream fixes.** A fix that would also help upstream (lean4-hash, lean-miniscript) goes in the committed `docs/upstream-fixes.md` (file, problem, fix), not in a br comment. Phase 10a (3 of 3) turns that file into patches.

## Spec refs
plan.md §1 (Curve ops, C code), §3 (Exactly one OpenSSL; Lake linking), §4 (Phase 1a row).

- Its contract:
  - it matches a request on method, path (including the query string, which Phase 9b's callback `amount=…&comment=…` and Phase 9d's `?date=` need) and canonical-JSON body, and serves an ordered list of responses per match. Canonical JSON means keys sorted and numbers compared as exact decimals (`0.1` = `0.10` = `1e-1`);
  - for JSON-RPC it matches path plus `method` plus canonical `params`, ignoring `id` and `jsonrpc`, and a recording entry may list several `params` variants mapped to one response. cyberkrill sends `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":"cyberkrill",…}` (`bitcoin_rpc.rs:434-439`) with f64 amounts, the port sends exact decimals, and the generator's own client sends a third shape;
  - a recording entry may state the `Authorization` header it expects; a request without it, or with another, gets that entry's 401 (Phase 8a (2 of 2) tests cookie and user/password auth this way);
  - it loads the recording files a test names, so each test serves only its own cases (Phase 8a (1 of 2) writes one file per case);
  - it has a fixed-port mode, for captures that need a known URL;
  - in fixed-port mode, a port already in use is a start-up error: the stub exits non-zero without printing its ready line, and the launcher fails the test instead of returning a port (Phases 9b and 9c rely on this on the host);
  - its recording file format is documented in README;
  - an unmatched request gets status 599 with a JSON body naming its method, path and body, and is logged to stderr; never 404, which feed parsers read as "no quote". After an entry's last ordered response it answers 599 "exhausted" (or repeats the last response if the entry says `repeat: true`);
  - it appends every request it receives to a request log the test can read;
  - README documents the command line (recording files, `--tls`, `--port`), the ready line it prints with the bound port, and how it stops.
- A Lean launcher (start, wait for the ready line, return the port, stop) lives in a `lean_lib HttpCurlTestSupport` in `packages/http-curl`, which `packages/cyberkrill` tests import. The launcher locates the stub script relative to the `http-curl` package (`../http-curl/test/…` from `packages/cyberkrill`), a layout the check derivation's source keeps (`flake.nix` takes all of `./packages`, and each package's tests run from its own directory). - The C wrapper, the Lean API and the CA logic (Phase 1b, 1 of 2).
- Recording anything: Phase 8a (1 of 2) writes the RPC recordings, and Phase 9 writes its synthetic fixtures.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- **No internet in tests.** The stub listens only on `127.0.0.1`.
- Do not commit a private key (AGENTS.md safety rule): the certificate and key are generated at test time, as in Phase 1b (1 of 2).

## Dependencies / ordering

- Phase 8a (1 of 2), Phase 9a (1 of 2), Phase 9c and Phase 9d wait for both Phase 1b beads, and the other Phase 8 and 9 beads wait through them.

title: Phase 1b (1 of 2): http-curl package (C wrapper over libcurl plus a Lean interface)
description:
## Outcome
`packages/http-curl` provides HTTPS and HTTP requests to Lean:
- a ~100-line C wrapper over nix libcurl (OpenSSL backend);
- a small Lean interface with GET and POST, request headers, HTTP basic auth, a bounded response size, connect and total timeouts, and structured errors;
- a working CA bundle on any Linux host.

## Why this exists
Owner decision (2026-10-18): Lean 4.35 has no HTTP client in core, so we write our own thin libcurl wrapper. Its Lean interface is small enough for Lean core's own client to replace it later. Every network command in v1 goes through it:
- Bitcoin Core JSON-RPC: plain HTTP to localhost with basic auth (Phase 8);
- price feeds, LNURL-pay and Fedimint config fetch over HTTPS (Phase 9).

Phase 1b is split in two to keep each Run small: this wrapper, its CA logic and their tests on a minimal localhost responder, then the reusable recording stub server (2 of 2).

## Scope
- C wrapper and Lean bindings in `packages/http-curl`. The libcurl link target from Phase 1a's spike lives here.
- The Lean API covers:
  - method GET or POST, URL, a header list, an optional body, optional basic-auth user and password;
  - a maximum response size, a connect timeout and a total timeout.
  - The result is the status code, the response headers (or at least content type), and the body bytes, or a structured error.
- Error kinds at least: DNS/connect failure, timeout, TLS/certificate failure, response larger than the limit, and other curl errors carrying their curl code and message.
  - An HTTP status of 4xx/5xx is a normal result, not an error. Callers decide.
- **CA fix.** A nix-built binary otherwise finds no CA bundle on non-NixOS hosts.
  - Lean 4.35 core has no CA-path list to reuse. Probe a fixed list of common bundle paths (for example `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt`, `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`), listed in README. Do not embed nix's cacert bundle: plan §2 allows either, and the probe list is the one chosen, so the binary carries no MPL-2.0 data (`pkgs.cacert`'s `meta.license.spdxId` at the pinned nixpkgs) and Phase 10a (2 of 3)'s empty-root run exercises the probe path.
  - Always honour `SSL_CERT_FILE` when it is set. The wrapper reads `SSL_CERT_FILE` on each request, not once at start-up.
  - When `SSL_CERT_FILE` is unset or empty, no test hook is set and no probe path exists, the wrapper returns the certificate error without sending a request, so it never falls through to curl's `--with-ca-fallback`.
  - A test-only hook replaces the fallback, so tests can exercise it without touching the host's bundle. The hook is a field of the Lean request config (for example `caFallback : Option System.FilePath`), set only by tests; no environment variable, so the release binary has none.
  - The wrapper always sets `CURLOPT_CAINFO` itself: `SSL_CERT_FILE` if set and non-empty, else the fallback (the test hook's path when set, otherwise the first existing probe path). It never relies on OpenSSL's default verify paths.
  - Why: the pinned nixpkgs' `setup.sh` (`pkgs/stdenv/generic/setup.sh:1004-1009`) exports `NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE=/no-cert-file.crt` and `SSL_CERT_FILE=/no-cert-file.crt` unless `IN_NIX_SHELL` is `impure`, so in the check sandbox `SSL_CERT_FILE` is never unset by default. nixpkgs OpenSSL carries `nix-ssl-cert-file.patch`, curl is built with `--with-ca-fallback` (`curlMinimal/package.nix:199`), and the toolchain's static OpenSSL is unpatched.
  - Each CA case runs in a child process whose environment sets or removes **both** `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE` explicitly (`IO.Process.spawn` env entries with `none` remove a variable). Run the CA tests both in `nix develop` and in `nix flake check`.
- **A minimal localhost responder for these tests**, over plain HTTP and over TLS with a self-signed certificate: it echoes a body and headers, answers a 401 to wrong basic-auth credentials, sends an oversized body, and stalls. It lives under `packages/http-curl/test/`, and Phase 1b (2 of 2) grows it into the reusable stub server.
  - Its interpreter and `openssl` are added to `devShells.default` (the common DoD also runs `nix develop -c lake test`) and to the check derivation, whose source is only `lean-toolchain` plus `packages/` and whose `nativeBuildInputs` is only `lean` today. Name the interpreter in README, for example `python3` with `http.server` and `ssl`, so one implementation serves both HTTP and TLS.
- Switch the `HttpCurlTests` driver to a `lean_exe` so the tests run.

## Non-goals
- The reusable recording stub server: request matching, JSON-RPC `params` variants, recorded `Authorization` entries, ordered responses, fixed-port mode and the recording format (Phase 1b, 2 of 2).
- JSON-RPC, price-feed, LNURL or Fedimint logic (Phases 8 and 9).
- WebSockets. Fedimint `wss://` URLs are rewritten to `https://` by the app (Phase 9).
- Cookies, redirects beyond what libcurl's defaults need, HTTP/2 tuning, proxies.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- **Exactly one OpenSSL** in the final executable. Keep Phase 1a's resolution; re-check with `ldd`/`nm` on an executable that uses the wrapper.
- **No internet in tests.** Use only the localhost responder. The nix sandbox allows loopback, and `nix flake check` must run these tests.
- Generate the self-signed test certificate and key at test time (for example with nix's `openssl`). Do not commit a private key (AGENTS.md safety rule). The certificate carries `subjectAltName = IP:127.0.0.1, DNS:localhost` (for example `openssl req -x509 … -addext "subjectAltName=IP:127.0.0.1,DNS:localhost"`): Phase 9b and Phase 10a (2 of 3) connect to `https://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Phase 1b (2 of 2)'s stub reuses this generation step.
- Never log or echo basic-auth credentials in errors.
- The size limit must abort the transfer rather than buffer an unbounded body.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Plan §4: Phase 1b depends on Phase 1a, so this bead waits for both Phase 1a beads. It uses Phase 1a (1 of 2)'s libcurl link target and OpenSSL resolution.
- Phase 1b (2 of 2) waits for this bead. Phases 8 (Core RPC) and 9 (HTTPS commands) wait for both Phase 1b beads.

## Acceptance Criteria
Localhost tests, each watched red once against a broken wrapper:
- GET and POST round-trip a body and headers.
- Basic auth: the right credentials succeed, the wrong ones get the responder's 401 as a normal result.
- A response over the size limit produces the size error.
- A stub that stalls produces the timeout error within the configured bound.
- A closed port produces the connect error.
- TLS:
  - with `SSL_CERT_FILE` pointing at the self-signed CA, an HTTPS request to the TLS responder succeeds;
  - without it, the request fails with the certificate error;
  - CA fallback, through the test hook: with `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `NIX_SSL_CERT_FILE` both removed and the hook pointed at the test CA, the request succeeds; pointed at a missing path, it fails with the certificate error;
  - each CA case passes both in `nix develop` and in `nix flake check`.
- `ldd`/`nm` evidence of one OpenSSL, recorded in README.
### Common definition of done (plan §4, every Run)

title: Phase 3a (4 of 4): scriptPubKey to address and back (P2PKH, P2SH, P2WPKH, P2WSH, P2TR) per network
description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin` converts between a scriptPubKey and its address string for P2PKH, P2SH, P2WPKH, P2WSH and P2TR, on each network cyberkrill supports. Per-type round-trip theorems are proven, BIP350's segwit address vectors and BIP173's v0 ones pass, and BIP173's three bech32 v1+ addresses are rejected. This bead completes Phase 3a.

## Why this exists
Every app command that prints or accepts an address goes through this:
- `onchain-decode-psbt` outputs;
- the UTXO listing;
- PSBT outputs;
- BOLT11 fallback addresses.

## Scope
- A network type covering mainnet, testnet, signet and regtest. Check cyberkrill's `Network` usage for exactly which networks it accepts.
- Base58Check versions:
  - P2PKH 0x00 on mainnet, 0x6f otherwise;
  - P2SH 0x05 on mainnet, 0xc4 otherwise.
- Segwit hrps: `bc`, `tb` (testnet and signet), `bcrt`.
- Witness rules (BIP141/BIP350):
  - v0 programs are 20 or 32 bytes, encoded with bech32;
  - v1+ programs are 2-40 bytes, encoded with bech32m.
  - The BIP350 valid vectors include unknown witness versions up to 16, so handle generic witness programs for those vectors, not only P2TR.
- Script templates: P2PKH, P2SH, `OP_0 <20>`, `OP_0 <32>`, `OP_1 <32>`, and generic `OP_n <program>`.

## Non-goals
- Descriptors. Bitcoin Core handles them through RPC in Phase 8.
- Address derivation from public keys (no hash160 here).

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Decoding an address checks it against the expected network and reports a mismatch distinctly.
- The bech32 layer is called with the 90-character limit.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on Phase 3a (1 of 4) for hex, Phase 3a (2 of 4) for Base58Check, and Phase 3a (3 of 4) for bech32/m.
- With those three, this bead completes Phase 3a, which Phases 3b, 4a-4d, 5 and 6 wait for.

## Acceptance Criteria
Theorems, with `#print axioms`:
- address ↔ script round-trip for each type, for example `toScript (fromScript s net) = s` for each supported template, and the reverse direction over lower-case address strings or over the parsed address value. It is false on raw strings: BIP173 L306 and BIP350 L186 are upper case, and encoding returns lower case.

Tests (state the counts: BIP350 segwit valid 8 and invalid 15; BIP173 v0 valid 3, all also in BIP350's list (L306, L307, L311 = L186, L187, L191), v1+ rejected 3, invalid 10; Base58 22). Each vector file's provenance line names source URL, commit, path and licence: BIP173/350 @ `130b8e0`, BSD-2-Clause; Core `key_io_valid.json` @ `9be056a`, MIT.

description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin` gains our own base58 encoder and decoder, using the Bitcoin alphabet and keeping leading zero bytes as leading `1`s. It also gains Base58Check: payload plus a 4-byte SHA-256d checksum. Both carry proofs.

`packages/bitcoin` gains our own bech32 (BIP173) and bech32m (BIP350) encoder and decoder, plus the 8-bit ↔ 5-bit regrouping (`convertbits`) that segwit addresses, BOLT11, LNURL and Fedimint invites all use. Round-trip and checksum-soundness theorems are proven.

- The polymod checksum, hrp expansion, checksum creation and verification for both constants:

- Encode `(hrp, data : List of 5-bit values, variant)` to a string, and decode a string to `(hrp, data, variant)`.

    - hrp characters outside 33-126;
    - a missing separator;
    - characters outside the charset;

`packages/bitcoin` gains three codecs:
- **hex** encode and decode;

- an exact **`Amount`** type held in millisatoshis, with BTC, sats and msats parsing and printing that never uses floating point.

Their round-trip and exactness theorems are proven.

## Why this exists
Every later `bitcoin`, `lightning` and app bead builds on these:
- CompactSize frames transactions and PSBTs.

  - Decoding reports truncated input.
- `Amount` in msat, with:
  - constructors and accessors for BTC, sats and msats;
  - parse and print of decimal BTC (up to 11 fractional digits, since 1 msat = 1e-11 BTC), sats (up to 3 fractional digits) and integer msats;
  - rejection of sub-msat precision.

Name each one as accepted or rejected, test each by name, and list every rejection under README "Deltas taken" (create that section if it is missing; Phase 7a extends it).
- Switch the `BitcoinTests` driver from a built-only `lean_lib` to a `lean_exe`, so `lake test` runs the vectors.

## Non-goals
- Transaction and PSBT serialization (Phase 4a, copied from lean-miniscript).
- Fiat conversion (Phase 9a).

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- **Overlap with Phase 4a.** lean-miniscript @ `cb9bc5f` has its own `compactSize` in `LeanMiniscript/Bitcoin/Serialization.lean`, and a decoder with proofs in `Deserialization.lean` and `DeserializationProofs.lean`. Phase 4a (1 of 3) copies those files.
  - Take that code under the copy rules (provenance comment, MIT notice beside it), unless a reason to write our own is recorded in README. `Deserialization.lean` imports `LegacySighash` and through it `LeanHash160`, the chain Phase 4a (1 of 3) cuts, so copy slices into one module: `Bitcoin/Serialization.lean` whole (it imports only `Lean`), `Deserialization.lean` L11-79 (`DecodeError` … `decodeAll`: no tx types, no hashing) and the matching `DeserializationProofs.lean` lemmas L7-179 (`unsignedLE_length` … `readCompactSize_ok`, which ends before `readByteVector_ok` at L180). The slices use nothing outside themselves except the namespace header. The provenance comment names the line ranges, and Phase 4a (1 of 3) imports this module and copies only the remaining lines.
  - Upstream's `readCompactSize` already rejects non-minimal encodings (`Deserialization.lean:33-45`, `.nonCanonicalCompactSize`), and its round-trip `readCompactSize_compactSize` and `readCompactSize_ok` (accepted bytes are `compactSize value ++ rest`, which gives canonicity) are proven (`DeserializationProofs.lean:31`, `:117`).
  - Phase 4a (1 of 3) owns the final reconcile: `bitcoin` must end Phase 4a with a single CompactSize codec, and README says which one is canonical.
- Parsers return errors and never panic.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Plan §4: Phase 3a depends on Phase 2, so this bead does too (even though these three codecs don't hash).
- Phase 3a (2 of 4) waits for this bead (the base58 vectors are hex), and so does Phase 3a (4 of 4, address ↔ script).

Theorems, each listed with `#print axioms`:
- **CompactSize and serialization:** round-trip for `n < 2^64`, `decode (encode n) = some (n, [])` (or the equivalent with a remainder), and a rejection theorem for non-canonical encodings.   - sub-msat precision rejected.

title: Phase 3b (2 of 2): bech32/bech32m 4-error detection theorem, per variant (data part of at most 89 characters)
description:
## Outcome
A proven theorem, in `bitcoin`, or, if the proof needs Mathlib, in a new `bitcoin-proofs` package (plan §6 #2). It states, **per variant**, as BIP173 "Checksum" and BIP350 claim it: for a string valid under variant v (bech32 or bech32m) whose data part is **at most 89 characters**, **any substitution of 1 to 4 data characters yields a string that variant v's checksum verification rejects**.

## Why this exists
This is the headline checksum guarantee at proof level M: checksums catch the errors their specification says they catch. Addresses are at most 90 characters, so the guarantee covers every address the port handles.

## Scope
- Follow the proof plan that Phase 3b (1 of 2) committed. Read its verdict first.
- State the theorem over Phase 3a (3 of 4)'s exact `polymod` and decoder. Do not prove it about a separate model unless the model is proven equal to the code.
- "Data characters" means every character after the separator, checksum included (BIP173's "data part"). A substitution replaces a data character by another bech32 charset character, so the hrp, the separator position and the case are unchanged.
- The statement in Lean: for each variant `v`, every hrp `h`, and all data vectors `d`, `d'` with `∀ x ∈ d ++ d', x < 32` (or Phase 3a (3 of 4)'s 5-bit element type, such as `Fin 32`), of equal length with `6 ≤ d.length ≤ 89` (the data part including its 6 checksum symbols): if `verifyChecksum v h d = true` and `d` and `d'` differ in at least 1 and at most 4 positions, then `verifyChecksum v h d' = false`.
- Corollary over the real decoder: if `s`'s data part has at most 89 characters (in particular, any `s` that `decode` accepts with the address limit 90) and `s` decodes with variant `v`, and `t` differs from `s` in 1 to 4 data-part positions, each replaced by a charset character, then `decode t` (with the same limit) does not return variant `v`. In Lean, the 1-4 positions are those where the charset index of `toLower t[i]` differs from that of `toLower s[i]`, and `t` agrees with `s` at every other position. A character-level reading is false: `019PYQ3G7` and `019pyq3g7` are both valid bech32 and differ in 4 positions, each by a charset character.
- Both bounds are needed, and neither is a weakening. Without the length bound the corollary is false: `a1gys8lu7cdxlpcmqu3wx5pppqcdmpwulwkwwajp6xtj84mvnjlez70e6thh9ux2ehlp7zne22wqvwekka3qcgxcsphe` and `a1hys8lu7cdxtpcmqu3wx5pppqcdmpwulwkwwajp6xtj84mvnjlez70e6thh9ux2ehlp7zne22wqv0ekka3qcgxcsphn` (92 characters, data part 90) are both valid bech32, 4 substitutions apart, and `a1dmr7hv6lk6kq4apwtt9szy9puq3038tkjy22s23ja5l78pnc46vsxsdmpwpefz2umwuwpe5mrngdrnyynn26xapf2c` / `a1jmr7hv6lk6zq4apwtt9szy9puq3038tkjy22s23ja5l78pnc46vsxsdmpwpefz2umwuwpe5mrngvrnyynn26xapf2j` are a bech32m pair. Without `x < 32` it is false at 2 positions: `a12uel5l` has data `[10,28,25,31,20,31]`, and `[10,28,24,63,20,31]` gives the same `polymod`.
- Cover both variants (bech32 and bech32m). `polymod`'s linear part is shared by both, so one finite fact can cover the two (Phase 3b (1 of 2)'s plan).
- This per-variant statement corrects a false earlier wording ("any substitution of at most 4 data characters is rejected by the decoder", across both variants); it is a correction, not a weakening, and plan §2 states it the same way.
- Only if Phase 3b (1 of 2)'s plan needs Mathlib: create `packages/bitcoin-proofs`, which requires `bitcoin` plus Mathlib through a pinned flake input (the sandbox cannot fetch it). Add it to `lakePackages` in `flake.nix`. Its lakefile carries `license := "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` and `licenseFiles := #["../../LICENSE-MIT", "../../LICENSE-APACHE"]`, like the other seven. Keep `bitcoin` itself Mathlib-free (plan §2). Update AGENTS.md's package count, README's package table and plan §2's diagram to include it.

## Non-goals
- BOLT11, LNURL and invites. They exceed 90 characters, so they only get round-trip and checksum soundness (plan §6 default #2).
- Burst errors, insertions and deletions. They are not part of the statement.
- **Cross-variant acceptance** is not covered, and is false: 4 substitutions turn the valid bech32 string `bc1qw508d6qejxtdg4y5r3zarvary0c5xw7kv8f3t4` (BIP173's P2WPKH example) into the valid bech32m string `bc1qw508d6qejxtdg4y5r3zarvary0c5uw7ka8f3x3` (indices 32, 36, 40, 41).
- **The segwit address decoder's witness-version rules** are not covered: changing the version character `q`→`p` plus 3 more substitutions gives `bc1pw508s6qejrtdg4y5r3zarvary0c5xwykv8f3t4`, a valid bech32m string that BIP350's reference `decode("bc", …)` accepts as witness version 1 with a 20-byte program.

title: Phase 3b (1 of 2): feasibility spike for the bech32/bech32m 4-error detection theorem
description:
## Outcome
A committed proof plan for the 4-error theorem that Phase 3b (2 of 2) proves, plus one proven reduction lemma over Phase 3a (3 of 4)'s real `polymod` and decoder, with its kernel checking cost measured. The spike ends with a verdict: is the full theorem in reach inside the time budget, and does it need Mathlib (and so `bitcoin-proofs`)?

## Why this exists
The theorem is the headline checksum guarantee at proof level M, and the riskiest proof in v1:
- BIP173's bound for data parts of up to 89 characters most likely comes from a computer search, not a short argument;
- a kernel `decide` over that search space may be infeasible;
- if the proof needs Mathlib, plan §6 #2 puts it in a new `bitcoin-proofs` package. Mathlib cannot be fetched inside the nix sandbox, so it would come in as a pinned flake input, the package would be listed in `lakePackages`, and the sorry grep keeps `--exclude-dir=.lake`. Mathlib's build time in the sandbox then counts against the budget below.

A short spike settles this before a full Run is spent on it. **Launch its Run with `--max-rounds 3`.**

## Scope
- The statement that Phase 3b (2 of 2) proves (plan §2, as corrected), **per variant**, as BIP173 and BIP350 claim it: for a string valid under variant v (bech32 or bech32m) whose data part is **at most 89 characters**, any substitution of 1 to 4 data characters yields a string that variant v's checksum verification rejects.
  - "Data characters" means every character after the separator, checksum included (BIP173's "data part"). A substitution replaces a data character by another bech32 charset character, so the hrp, the separator position and the case are unchanged.
  - In Lean, over Phase 3a (3 of 4)'s definitions: for each variant `v`, every hrp `h`, and all data vectors `d`, `d'` with `∀ x ∈ d ++ d', x < 32` (or Phase 3a (3 of 4)'s 5-bit element type, such as `Fin 32`), of equal length with `6 ≤ d.length ≤ 89` (the data part including its 6 checksum symbols): if `verifyChecksum v h d = true` and `d` and `d'` differ in at least 1 and at most 4 positions, then `verifyChecksum v h d' = false`.

In Lean, the 1-4 positions are those where the charset index of `toLower t[i]` differs from that of `toLower s[i]`, and `t` agrees with `s` at every other position. A character-level reading is false: `019PYQ3G7` and `019pyq3g7` are both valid bech32 and differ in 4 positions, each by a charset character.

Without the length bound the corollary is false: `a1gys8lu7cdxlpcmqu3wx5pppqcdmpwulwkwwajp6xtj84mvnjlez70e6thh9ux2ehlp7zne22wqvwekka3qcgxcsphe` and `a1hys8lu7cdxtpcmqu3wx5pppqcdmpwulwkwwajp6xtj84mvnjlez70e6thh9ux2ehlp7zne22wqv0ekka3qcgxcsphn` (92 characters, data part 90) are both valid bech32, 4 substitutions apart, and `a1dmr7hv6lk6kq4apwtt9szy9puq3038tkjy22s23ja5l78pnc46vsxsdmpwpefz2umwuwpe5mrngdrnyynn26xapf2c` / `a1jmr7hv6lk6zq4apwtt9szy9puq3038tkjy22s23ja5l78pnc46vsxsdmpwpefz2umwuwpe5mrngvrnyynn26xapf2j` are a bech32m pair. Without `x < 32` it is false at 2 positions: `a12uel5l` has data `[10,28,25,31,20,31]`, and `[10,28,24,63,20,31]` gives the same `polymod`.
  - The earlier wording ("any substitution of at most 4 data characters is rejected by the decoder", across both variants) is false; see Non-goals. This restatement corrects a false statement and is not a weakening.
- A proof plan, committed as a doc under `packages/bitcoin/` (for example `docs/bech32-4-error-plan.md`). It gives the reduction steps from the decoder to a statement about `polymod`, the finite check left at the end, and how that check is done.
  - `polymod` is affine over GF(2), so a substitution pattern `e` changes the residue by a linear `L(e)` that depends only on each changed position's distance from the end, and both variants share `L`. State the final finite fact as "no nonzero weight-≤4 vector over positions < 89 has `L(e) = 0`". It is a pure statement about the linear map, and may suggest a BCH-bound route rather than enumeration.
- One reduction lemma from that plan, proven over the real `polymod` and decoder (not a model), with `#print axioms`.
- A measurement: the lemma's kernel time, and an estimate for the full finite check.

- The full theorem (Phase 3b, 2 of 2).

- No `native_decide` in the proof (plan §6 default #3).

title: Phase 4a (3 of 3): PSBT and transaction proofs: serialize/parse round-trips, duplicate-key and trailing-data rejection
description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin` proves, over the code Phase 4a (1 of 3) ported:
- `parse cap hashes (serialize p) = .ok p` for every PSBT `p` with `valid cap hashes p`, where `valid` is defined explicitly without `parse` or `serialize`;
- the PSBT parser rejects duplicate keys and trailing data;
- the transaction codec round-trips for transactions the wire format can carry (`Transaction.WellFormed`).

## Why this exists
Plan §2 lists the first two as `bitcoin`'s PSBT obligations. Its "CompactSize and serialization: round-trip" obligation covers transactions too, and no other bead owns that one.

## Scope
- **Copy** `LeanMiniscript/Psbt/CodecProofs.lean` and `Psbt/ParseProofs.lean` from lean-miniscript @ `cb9bc5f`, and port them. Build on them rather than reproving:
  - `Psbt.parse_serialize` (`ParseProofs.lean:31-34`) takes **two** hypotheses, `formed : psbt.WellFormed` and `decodes : psbt.decode = .ok decoded`, and concludes `Psbt.parse psbt.serialize = .ok psbt`. `Psbt.parse` is framing plus `psbt.decode`'s field validation (`Fields.lean:536-539`), and `decode` is where `validPublicKey` and `preimageHash` run (`Fields.lean:206-207`, `:272-276`). After Phase 4a (1 of 3), `parse` and `decode` take the pubkey capability `cap` and the preimage-hash parameter `hashes`.
  - `Psbt.serialize_parse` (`:40`): accepted bytes are `serialize` of a PSBT that is `WellFormed` and decodes.
- **Define `valid`** explicitly: `valid cap hashes p := p.WellFormed ∧ ∃ d, p.decode cap hashes = .ok d`. It may use the field decoder, never `parse` or `serialize`, and it matches `parse_serialize`'s two hypotheses. `WellFormed` alone is not enough: the round-trip is false for a PSBT with a key the capability rejects.
- Derive the duplicate-key and trailing-data rejections from `Psbt.serialize_parse` and `KeyValueMap.WellFormed`, which includes `Unique` (`Codec.lean:68-69`).
- Show that `valid` holds on every valid vector, using Phase 4a (1 of 3)'s test capability and stand-in hashes. No valid vector carries a RIPEMD160 or HASH160 field, so Phase 4a (2 of 3) is not needed for that.
- **The statements** (upstream has no transaction round-trip: `DeserializationProofs.lean` stops at CompactSize, byte vectors and witness stacks):
  - (a) `Psbt.parse cap hashes bytes = .ok p → p.global.Unique ∧ (∀ m ∈ p.inputs, m.Unique) ∧ ∀ m ∈ p.outputs, m.Unique` (from `serialize_parse` and `KeyValueMap.WellFormed`);
  - (b) `Psbt.parse cap hashes bytes = .ok p → Psbt.parse cap hashes (bytes ++ extra) = .ok q → extra = ByteArray.empty` (`Codec.lean:127` throws `.trailingData`);
  - (c) for `tx` with every `txid.size = 32`, every script and witness item size `< 2^64`, `tx.inputs.size < 2^64`, `tx.outputs.size < 2^64`, every witness stack's length `< 2^64`, `witnesses.length = tx.inputs.size`, and `tx.inputs.size > 0 ∨ tx.outputs.size = 0` (a 0-input, 0-output transaction round-trips through the zero-flag path, `Deserialization.lean:120-123`): `parseTransaction (serializeWitnessTransaction tx witnesses) = .ok ⟨tx, witnesses'⟩`, where `witnesses' = witnesses` if some stack is non-empty and `tx.inputs.toList.map (fun _ => [])` otherwise.
  - State (c)'s hypotheses as a named `Transaction.WellFormed`. They are inherent to the wire format, not a weakening, and README lists them. The size and count bounds are there because CompactSize carries at most 2^64 − 1 (upstream's `readCompactSize_compactSize` takes `value < 2 ^ 64`, `DeserializationProofs.lean:31`): an `Array` of 2^64 outputs serializes its count as `ff 00…00`, which `readCompactSize` rejects as non-canonical. The unconditional form is false: `readTransaction (allowWitness := true)` reads an empty input vector as the BIP144 marker (`Deserialization.lean:115-147`), `readOutPoint` takes exactly 32 bytes while `txid` is a `ByteArray`, and `serializeWitnessTransaction` treats missing stacks as empty and emits the legacy form when all are empty (`:159-170`).

## Non-goals
- New parser features. RIPEMD-160 and HASH160 (Phase 4a, 2 of 3).
- PSBT role modules.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- **Never weaken a stated obligation.** If one is out of reach, follow the common stop mechanics.
- Copied files get the common provenance comment (upstream files carry no per-file header); lean-miniscript's MIT notice sits beside them.

title: Phase 4a (2 of 3): our own RIPEMD-160 and HASH160 in bitcoin, used by the PSBT preimage checks
description:
## Outcome
`packages/bitcoin` has its own RIPEMD-160, about 130 lines, and HASH160 = RIPEMD-160(SHA-256(x)) using `packages/sha256`. Both pass the published vectors. The PSBT parser's RIPEMD160 and HASH160 preimage checks go through them, so a PSBT whose preimage does not match its key is rejected.

## Why this exists
Owner decision (2026-10-19), which closed the RIPEMD-160 question bead: write our own RIPEMD-160 in `bitcoin`, under the repo's MIT OR Apache-2.0 header.
- The copied parser checks `PSBT_IN_RIPEMD160` and `PSBT_IN_HASH160` preimages (`LeanMiniscript/Psbt/Fields.lean` @ `cb9bc5f` L272-276, validated at L401-411). lean4-hash carries no RIPEMD-160, so "hash through `sha256`" cannot cover them.
- `febyeji/lean-hash160` is **not** copied. It is Apache-2.0 only, which would make `bitcoin` and every package above it "(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Apache-2.0", against plan §5 and §6 #7.
- Skipping the check would break parity: rust-bitcoin 0.32.8, which cyberkrill uses, rejects bad RIPEMD160 and HASH160 preimages.

## Scope
- `ripemd160 : ByteArray → ByteArray` (20 bytes), written from the algorithm's published description, and `hash160 b = ripemd160 (sha256 b)`.
- New files carry the dual-licence header. Copy no code from lean-hash160 or any other RIPEMD-160 implementation.
- Fill Phase 4a (1 of 3)'s preimage-hash parameter with these two functions, so the PSBT parser that `bitcoin` exports checks all four preimage key types.

## Non-goals
- A proof that the implementation matches the specification. There is no RIPEMD-160 obligation at level M.
- Any other use of HASH160, such as deriving addresses from public keys.

## Critical constraints and failure handling
- Pure Lean, no FFI.
- A preimage mismatch is a structured parser error, distinct from the other PSBT errors.

## Dependencies / ordering
- Depends on Phase 4a (1 of 3), whose parser takes the parameter, and on the RIPEMD-160 decision bead (closed).
- Phase 7a and Phase 8a wait for all three Phase 4a beads.

## Acceptance Criteria
- **RIPEMD-160 vectors**: the 9 messages of the algorithm authors' published list (the RIPEMD-160 page of Dobbertin, Bosselaers and Preneel): `""`, `"a"`, `"abc"`, `"message digest"`, `"a…z"`, the 56-character `"abcdbcde…nopq"` string, the 62-character `"A…Za…z0…9"` string, 8 × `"1234567890"`, and one million `"a"`. All 9 pass, and the test prints the count.
  - The page states no licence, so under the third-party rule no digest is copied from it. A committed script computes the 9 expected digests with nix `openssl dgst -ripemd160` (OpenSSL 3.5.8 at the pinned nixpkgs provides it) and writes the vector file, whose provenance line names the script and cites the page by URL only. README says the digests equal the page's list.
- **HASH160:** the hash160 of the public key in BIP173's P2WPKH example equals that example's 20-byte witness program.
- **PSBT:** for each of the RIPEMD160 and HASH160 key types, a matching preimage is accepted and a one-byte change is rejected with the preimage error. Any vector that Phase 4a (1 of 3) listed as waiting for these checks now passes.
